title: Feelings & support
goal: Ask a friend what's wrong, comfort and reassure them, apologise properly, congratulate good news and offer condolences — and join events with 'while', 'as soon as', 'until' and 'before'.
intro:
When a friend is down, Pashto has warm, ready-made words for it: **خير خو دی؟** 'is everything OK?', **غم مه کوه** 'don't worry', **ډاډه اوسه** 'rest assured'. Good news is met with **مبارک دې شه!** (and a demand for sweets); bad news with a blessing for the dead and patience for the living.

In this unit you'll learn to talk about feelings the Pashto way — anger, laughter and tears **come to you** (غوسه مې راغله 'I got angry') — to tell someone kindly *not* to do something (مه ژاړه 'don't cry'), and to link events in time with **کله چې** 'while', **څنګه چې** 'as soon as', **تر هغه چې** 'until' and **مخکې له دې چې** 'before'.

grammar.title: While, as soon as, until, before: time clauses
grammar.body:
Pashto joins two events in time with a word + **چې**. The time clause comes **first**, with its own verb at its end, and the main sentence follows.

**کله چې … 'when / while'.** With the **imperfective** past it means 'while I was …-ing': کله چې زه کور ته **تلم**، … 'while I was going home, …' (تلم tlə́m 'I was going'). With the perfective past it is a plain 'when': کله چې ورسېدم 'when I arrived'. The news and formal Pashto also use **په داسې حال کې چې** 'while, whereas'.

**څنګه چې … 'as soon as'** (lit. 'how that') + perfective: څنګه چې خبر **شوم**، راغلم 'as soon as I heard, I came'. In casual speech you'll also hear **همدا چې**.

**تر هغه چې … 'until'** + subjunctive: تر هغه چې ته **راشې**، زه دلته يم 'I'm here until you come'.

**مخکې له دې چې … 'before'** + subjunctive: مخکې له دې چې **ووځې** … 'before you go out …'. ('After' is **وروسته له دې چې** + past.)

**The trap**: for a future event English uses the present ('as soon as I *arrive*'). Pashto uses the **subjunctive** (the perfective present, no به) in the time clause, and puts **به** only in the main clause: څنګه چې **ورسېږم**، زنګ **به** درته ووهم.

grammar.title: Feelings that come to you: غوسه مې راغله
grammar.body:
In English *you* get angry or feel like crying. Pashto often makes the **feeling** the subject: it **comes to you** (راځي), and a clitic (مې، دې، يې، مو) says who it comes to:

خوب **مې** راځي 'I'm sleepy' (lit. sleep comes to me) · غوسه **مې** راځي 'I'm getting angry' · خندا **مې** راځي 'I can't help laughing' · ژړا **مې** راځي 'I feel like crying'.

In the past the verb **agrees with the feeling, not with you**: خوب مې **راغی** (خوب m) · غوسه مې **راغله** (f) · اوښکې مې **راغلې** (f pl) 'tears came to my eyes'. Change the clitic to change the person: غوسه **يې** راغله 'he/she got angry', ولې **دې** خندا راغله؟ 'why did you laugh?'. Like all clitics, it sits after the first word or phrase.

The heart (زړه) does a lot of feeling too: زړه مې **تنګ** دی 'I'm feeling down', زړه مې **مات** شو 'I was hurt', زړه مې پرې **سوځي** 'I feel so sorry for him'.

With an **adjective + کېدل**, by contrast, *you* become the feeling and the adjective agrees with you: حيران شوم (a man) / **حيرانه** شوم (a woman) 'I was amazed'.

examples.en: I'm getting sleepy — I'm off to bed.

examples.native: زړه مې پرې سوځي، ډېر يوازې دی.
examples.roman: zṛə me pre swádzi, ḍer yawā́ze day.
examples.en: I feel so sorry for him, he's all alone.

grammar.title: Kind 'don'ts': مه + the imperfective
grammar.body:
To tell someone **not** to do something, put **مه** (ma) before the verb and use the **imperfective** imperative — never the و- (perfective) form:

وخوره 'eat!' → **مه خوره** 'don't eat' · ووايه 'say it!' → **مه وايه** 'don't say it' · لاړ شه 'go!' → **مه ځه** 'don't go'.

With compound verbs **مه** sits between the two parts: غم **مه** کوه 'don't worry' (lit. don't do grief), خفه **مه** کېږه 'don't be upset', فکر **مه** کوه 'don't think about it'.

Endings: **-a** to one friend (مه ژاړه 'don't cry'), **-əy** politely or to several people (مه ژاړئ، غم مه کوئ). With elders and at condolences, use the polite form.

The positive comforting commands use **اوسه** 'be, stay' (imperative of اوسېدل): **ډاډه اوسه** 'rest assured', **ټينګ اوسه** 'stay strong'; polite **اوسئ**. Soften any of these with the person's name or جانه / جانې: مه ژاړه، خورې جانې.

examples.en: Don't cry, I'm here with you.

examples.roman: xapá ma kéẓa, dā stā ġaltí na wa.

examples.roman: fikr ma kawa, sabā́ ba sam shi.
examples.en: Don't think about it, it'll be fine tomorrow.

lines.roman: ho kəna! malgartyā́ də hamdé wradzó lapā́ra da.
lines.en: Of course! That's what friends are for (lit. friendship is for days like these).

lines.roman: xandā́ me rā́ġla. manə́na, wróra, zṛə me ləẓ ṣə shu.
lines.en: You've made me laugh. Thanks, brother — I feel a bit better.

lines.speaker: Bilal
lines.native: ښه، اوس پاڅه. څنګه چې کور ته ورسېږو، ستا پلار ته به يې سره ووايو.
lines.roman: ṣə, os pā́tsa. tsə́nga che kor ta wə́raseẓu, stā plār ta ba ye sara wə́wāyu.
lines.en: Right, get up. As soon as we get to your place, we'll tell your dad together.

lines.speaker: Wahid
lines.native: سمه ده. خدای دې خير درکړي، وروره.
lines.roman: sáma da. xudā́y de xayr dárkṛi, wróra.

culture:
Pashtuns check on each other directly: **خير خو دی؟** is the natural question when a friend looks low or calls at an odd hour, and comfort tends to be practical — 'I'm with you', 'we'll go together', 'I'll study with you' — rather than a long talk about feelings. Between friends of your age use ته and the short forms (غم مه کوه، ډاډه اوسه); to elders, to a friend's parents and at any condolence switch to تاسو (غم مه کوئ، ډاډه اوسئ).

**Good news**: say **مبارک دې شه** to one friend and **مبارک مو شه** to a family, add **ماشاالله**, and expect the cry **شيريني!** ('sweets!') — whoever passes an exam, gets a job or gets engaged is expected to treat everyone. Praise to someone's face is often wrapped in ماشاالله to ward off the evil eye (نظر).

**A death**: people go to the family's home or the mosque for the **فاتحه**, usually over the first three days; men and women sit separately. No speech is needed: shake hands or put your hand on your heart, say **خدای دې وبښي** for the person who died and **خدای دې صبر درکړي** to the family, raise your hands for a short silent prayer, and sit for a while. Say **وفات شو** 'passed away' rather than مړ شو 'died'. Neighbours send food to the bereaved family, and music and celebrations in the street pause for some days.

tip.title: Feelings come to you: غوسه مې راځي
tip.body:
- Pashto often makes the **feeling** the subject: غوسه **مې** راځي 'I'm getting angry' (lit. anger comes to me).
- The clitic says who: مې (me), دې (you), يې (him/her).
- In the past the verb agrees with the **feeling**: غوسه مې **راغله** (f), خوب مې **راغی** (m), اوښکې مې **راغلې** (pl).

lessons.title: Comforting a friend

tip.title: Don't …: مه + imperfective
tip.body:
- **مه** + the *imperfective* imperative: مه ژاړه 'don't cry', مه ځه 'don't go', مه وايه 'don't say it'.
- Compound verbs: مه goes in the middle: غم **مه** کوه, خفه **مه** کېږه.
- One friend **-a**, polite or plural **-əy**: غم مه کوه / غم مه کوئ.
- Comfort with **اوسه** 'be, stay': ډاډه اوسه, ټينګ اوسه.

tip.title: Saying sorry like you mean it
tip.body:
- **بښنه غواړم** is the all-purpose 'sorry'. To a friend you've hurt: **ما وبښه** 'forgive me' (polite **ما وبښئ**).
- Own it: **زما غلطي وه** 'it was my fault', **قصداً مې نه دي کړي** 'I didn't mean to'.
- The kind reply: **پروا نه لري** or **پرېږده** 'never mind, forget it'.
- Hurt feelings are 'broken': زړه مې **مات** شو 'I was hurt'.

sentences.native: بښنه غواړم، پرون مې ستا زړه مات کړ.
sentences.roman: baṣə́na ġwā́ṛəm, parún me stā zṛə māt kaṛ.
sentences.en: I'm sorry I hurt your feelings yesterday.

sentences.native: وروره، ما وبښه، هسې مې وويل.
sentences.roman: wróra, mā wə́baṣa, háse me wə́wayəl.
sentences.en: Forgive me, brother, I didn't mean what I said.

sentences.native: زما غلطي وه، بيا به داسې ونه کړم.
sentences.roman: zmā ġaltí wa, biyā́ ba dā́se wə́na kṛəm.
sentences.en: It was my fault, I won't do it again.

sentences.native: دا کار مې قصداً نه دی کړی.
sentences.roman: dā kār me qasdán na day kaṛay.
sentences.en: I didn't do this on purpose.

sentences.native: پروا نه لري، هر څوک غلطي کوي.
sentences.roman: parwā́ na lári, har tsok ġaltí kawí.
sentences.en: Never mind, everyone makes mistakes.

sentences.native: پرېږده، هېڅ خبره نه ده.
sentences.roman: préẓda, hets xabə́ra na da.
sentences.en: Forget it, it's nothing.

sentences.native: پياله مې ماته کړه، بښنه غواړم.
sentences.roman: piyā́la me mā́ta kṛa, baṣə́na ġwā́ṛəm.
sentences.en: I broke the cup, I'm sorry.

sentences.native: که زما غلطي وي، ما وبښئ.
sentences.roman: ka zmā ġaltí wi, mā wə́baṣəy.
sentences.en: If it's my fault, please forgive me.

sentences.native: هغه قصداً ناوخته راغی.
sentences.roman: haġá qasdán nāwáxta rā́ġay.
sentences.en: He came late on purpose.

sentences.native: پرېږده يې، هغه هسې خبرې کوي.
sentences.roman: préẓda ye, haġá háse xabə́re kawí.
sentences.en: Let it go — he's just talking.

lessons.title: Congratulating

tip.title: Good news: مبارک دې شه!
tip.body:
- **مبارک دې شه!** to one friend; **مبارک مو شه!** to a family or politely.
- Add praise: **ماشاالله!**, **په تا وياړم!** 'I'm proud of you'.
- **کامياب شوم** 'I passed / I made it' — کامياب agrees: کاميابه شوه (she passed).
- Then the friendly demand: **شيريني!** 'treat us to sweets!'

new: مبارک دې شه! ډېره ښه خبره ده!

sentences.native: مبارک دې شه! ته کامياب شوې!
sentences.roman: mubā́rak de sha! tə kāmyā́b shwe!
sentences.en: Congratulations! You passed!

sentences.native: زما خور په ازموينه کې کاميابه شوه.
sentences.roman: zmā xor pə azmóyəna ke kāmyā́ba shwa.
sentences.en: My sister passed her exam.

sentences.native: موږ په خپل زوی وياړو.
sentences.roman: muẓ pə xpəl zoy wyā́ṛu.
sentences.en: We're proud of our son.

sentences.native: زه په خپلې خور وياړم.
sentences.roman: zə pə xpə́le xor wyā́ṛəm.
sentences.en: I'm proud of my sister.

sentences.native: هغه بيا ناکام شو، خو بل کال به کامياب شي.
sentences.roman: haġá biyā́ nākā́m shu, xo bəl kāl ba kāmyā́b shi.
sentences.en: He failed again, but next year he'll pass.

sentences.native: احمد ته مې مبارکي ورکړه.
sentences.roman: ahmád ta me mubārakí wárkṛa.
sentences.en: I congratulated Ahmad.

sentences.native: مبارک مو شه، ستاسو خوشالي زموږ خوشالي ده.
sentences.roman: mubā́rak mo sha, stāso xoshālí zmuẓ xoshālí da.
sentences.en: Congratulations to you all — your joy is our joy.

sentences.native: ماشاالله، ته ډېر ښه شاګرد يې!
sentences.roman: māshāllā́h, tə ḍer ṣə shāgə́rd ye!
sentences.en: Well done — you're a great student!

sentences.native: نوې دنده دې مبارک شه!
sentences.roman: náwe dánda de mubā́rak sha!
sentences.en: Congratulations on your new job!

tip.title: Time clauses: څنګه چې، تر هغه چې، مخکې له دې چې
tip.body:
- **څنګه چې** 'as soon as', **تر هغه چې** 'until', **مخکې له دې چې** 'before', **کله چې** + imperfective past 'while'.
- The time clause comes first, the main sentence second.
- For a future event, the time clause takes the **subjunctive** (no به): څنګه چې **ورسېږم**، زنګ **به** ووهم.

sentences.native: څنګه چې نتيجه راشي، ما ته زنګ ووهه.
sentences.roman: tsə́nga che natijá rā́shi, mā ta zang wə́waha.
sentences.en: Call me as soon as the result comes out.

sentences.native: څنګه چې خبر شوم، مور ته مې وويل.
sentences.roman: tsə́nga che xabár shwəm, mor ta me wə́wayəl.
sentences.en: As soon as I heard, I told my mother.

sentences.native: څنګه چې يې نتيجه وليده، خوشاله شوه.
sentences.roman: tsə́nga che ye natijá wə́lida, xoshā́la shwa.
sentences.en: As soon as she saw the result, she was overjoyed.

sentences.native: څنګه چې کار خلاص کړم، راځم.
sentences.roman: tsə́nga che kār xlās kṛəm, rā́dzəm.
sentences.en: I'll come as soon as I finish work.

sentences.native: تر هغه چې نتيجه راشي، زه ارام نه يم.
sentences.roman: tər haġə́ che natijá rā́shi, zə ārā́m na yəm.
sentences.en: I can't relax until the result is out.

sentences.native: تر هغه چې ته راشې، موږ ډوډۍ نه خورو.
sentences.roman: tər haġə́ che tə rā́she, muẓ ḍoḍə́y na xwru.
sentences.en: We won't eat until you come.

sentences.native: تر هغه چې جوړ شې، کور کې پاتې شه.
sentences.roman: tər haġə́ che joṛ she, kor ke pā́te sha.
sentences.en: Stay at home until you get better.

sentences.native: مخکې له دې چې ډوډۍ وخورو، لاسونه ومينځه.
sentences.roman: mə́xke la de che ḍoḍə́y wə́xwru, lāsúna wə́mindza.
sentences.en: Wash your hands before we eat.

sentences.native: مخکې له دې چې پلار دې خبر شي، ما ته ووايه.
sentences.roman: mə́xke la de che plār de xabár shi, mā ta wə́wāya.
sentences.en: Tell me before your dad finds out.

sentences.native: کله چې موږ ډوډۍ خوړله، برېښنا لاړه.
sentences.roman: kə́la che muẓ ḍoḍə́y xwaṛə́la, breṣnā́ lā́ṛa.
sentences.en: While we were eating, the power went off.

lessons.title: When someone has died

tip.title: Condolences
tip.body:
- Say **وفات شو / شوه** 'passed away', not مړ شو.
- Whenever the person is mentioned: **خدای دې وبښي**.
- To the family, always with تاسو: **خدای دې صبر درکړي**, **ستاسو په غم کې شريک يو**.
- Going to pay your respects is **فاتحې ته تلل**.

new: ستاسو په غم کې شريک يو.

sentences.native: د احمد پلار پرون وفات شو.
sentences.roman: də ahmád plār parún wafā́t shu.
sentences.en: Ahmad's father passed away yesterday.

sentences.native: د هغې انا وفات شوه، خدای دې وبښي.
sentences.roman: də haġé anā́ wafā́t shwa, xudā́y de wə́baṣi.
sentences.en: Her grandmother passed away, may she rest in peace.

sentences.native: سبا فاتحې ته ځو، ته هم راځې؟
sentences.roman: sabā́ fātihé ta dzu, tə ham rā́dze?
sentences.en: We're going to pay our respects tomorrow — are you coming too?

sentences.native: ډېر افسوس، هغه ډېر ښه سړی و.
sentences.roman: ḍer afsós, haġá ḍer ṣə saṛáy wə.
sentences.en: So sorry — he was a really good man.

sentences.native: ستاسو د پلار د وفات خبر مې واورېد.
sentences.roman: stāso də plār də wafā́t xabár me wā́wred.
sentences.en: I heard about your father's passing.

sentences.native: هغه ډېر ځوان و، زړه مې پرې سوځي.
sentences.roman: haġá ḍer dzwān wə, zṛə me pre swádzi.
sentences.en: He was so young — my heart goes out to him.

sentences.native: د هغه کورنۍ ته تسلي ورکړئ.
sentences.roman: də haġə́ kornə́y ta tasallí wárkṛəy.
sentences.en: Comfort his family. (polite)

sentences.native: بښنه غواړم چې فاتحې ته نه شوم راتلای.
sentences.roman: baṣə́na ġwā́ṛəm che fātihé ta na shwəm rātlā́y.
sentences.en: I'm sorry I couldn't come to the condolence gathering.

sentences.native: ستاسو مور ډېره مهربانه وه.
sentences.roman: stāso mor ḍéra mehrabā́na wa.
sentences.en: Your mother was very kind.

sentences.native: موږ ټول د هغه په غم کې شريک يو.
sentences.roman: muẓ ṭol də haġə́ pə ġam ke sharík yu.
sentences.en: We all share in his grief.
